    A Ghost in Your Ear

    7:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Also on other days Para salir

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    BrownstoneJAZZ FEST CONCERT SERIES

    7:30 PM · BrownstoneJAZZ, Bedford-Stuyvesant (West) · $55.30 · ↻ Also on other days Algo especial

    -Please read fully to enjoy- BrownstoneJAZZ WEEKEND up close and personal. Intimate acoustic room live concerts Fridays & Saturdays 7:30pm or 9:30pm Sundays 4pm or 6pm Experience the JazzFest in a restored 19th Century Victorian Brownstone located in Bedford Stuyvesant's Central Brooklyn Landmarked Historical Community. Where you will feel transported back to an earlier time period walking through the doors. BrownstoneJAZZ Ensasmbles present the best of yesteryear's jazz soldiers and today's jazz frontier musicians, swinging with the authentic jazz style. Something for everyone to enjoy. Bed Stuy, B'klyn and SugarHill, Harlem were both Jazz Hey Day Communities. When Ella Fitzgerald lyricized the song 'TAKE THE A TRAIN' connecting NYC's two jazz hubs. BrownstoneJAZZ invites you to the magic of music with Curator Debbie McClain and M.C., Bassist Eric Lemons hosting you as you uncover this old school jazz venue to enjoy a different jazz experience. Get your ticket for our private event. Both Eric and Debbie have been involved in the world of music entertainment for years presenting major artist. The list is long. They really know their way around the business. FOR A LIMITED TIME: Tables and seats have been limited. Make early purchases. We sell out fast. NOTES DRESS TO IMPRESS --- It's the Jazz Age! Casual Classy, Cocktail or vintage attire are encouraged. Leave the jeans, shorts, t-shirt, and hoodie at home. NO Athletic Wear, Tank Tops, or T-shirts in THE ROOM NO REFUNDS (no exceptions) ID is required NO PETS NO Shopping-bags or Backpacks in THE ROOM.

    Juilliard at The Apollo: Kind of Blue

    7:30 PM · The Apollo's Victoria Theater 1, Harlem (South) Para salir

    With a career defined by constant reinvention, Miles Davis continuously shaped and reshaped the sound of jazz, moving from bebop to cool jazz, post-bop to fusion, and beyond. His time in New York City, a hub of jazz innovation and culture, started with Juilliard. To mark the iconic alum's 100th birthday, Juilliard Jazz and the Apollo Theater present a series of multidisciplinary performances on the legendary Harlem stage, honoring some of Davis' landmark albums: Birth of the Cool, Bitches Brew, and Kind of Blue.

    The Conversation

    8:00 PM · Astor Place Theatre, Greenwich Village Para salir

    THE CONVERSATION follows Marcus (Tony Award-winner Joshua Henry) and Elle (Julia Harriman) from the electric spark of their first date to move-ins, milestones, and the slow accumulation of everything left unsaid. The score, written by Henry and Harriman, weaves soul, R&B, and modern pop into bold musical theater storytelling that is intimate, honest, and emotionally gripping. With a book by Nick Green and directed by Tony Award-winner Kenny Leon, The Conversation asks what it takes to choose love, even when it hurts, and what it takes to stay.

    Maria Schneider Orchestra

    8:30 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $45.76 Algo especial

    Maria Schneiders music has been hailed by critics as evocative, majestic, magical, heart-stoppingly gorgeous, and beyond categorization. She and her 18-member orchestra have performed at concert halls around the world and have received 7 GRAMMYs, many Jazz Journalist Awards, and numerous DOWNBEAT and JAZZTIMES Readers and Critics Polls. Schneiders music blurs the lines between genres, making her long list of commissioners quite varied, stretching from jazz to classical, and dance, even collaborating with David Bowie. She is among a small few to have received GRAMMYs in multiple genres, having received the award in both jazz and classical, as well as for her work with David Bowie. Shes holds honorary doctorates from the University of Minnesota and Eastman School of Music. In 2019, the National Endowment for the Arts bestowed on Schneider the nations highest honor in jazz, naming her an NEA Jazz Master.

His time in New York City, a hub of jazz innovation and culture, started with Juilliard. To mark the iconic alum's 100th birthday, Juilliard Jazz and the Apollo Theater present a series of multidisciplinary performances on the legendary Harlem stage, honoring some of Davis' landmark albums: Birth of the Cool, Bitches Brew, and Kind of Blue.

    A Ghost in Your Ear

    5:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Also on other days Para salir

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.

    Patrick Wolf: Tour Of The Beast with special guest Abhora

    6:30 PM · Drom, East Village · $45.25 Algo especial

    VIP INFO NOTE: VIP add-on must be purchased in addition to a concert ticket. The VIP add-on does not include concert entry. Check-in at 5:00PM VIP includes early entry and a sneak peek of soundcheck, a meet & greet with Patrick and an exclusive piece of art. Note, VIP requires check-in at 5:00PM. No refunds will be issued for late arrival, if you miss any part of the VIP experience. -- Patrick Wolf released his first E.P. at the age of 19, a groundbreaking debut of classical, folk, and electronic music that set the pace for a stellar decade, releasing seven self-produced and solely written albums and performing multiple laps around the globe on tour, amassing an ever-growing and dedicated, spellbound audience. A viola, piano, dulcimer, harp, lyre, and tenor guitar player, Patrick's decade of critically acclaimed work, touring, joining Patti Smith's band, collaborations with Florence Welch, Marianne Faithful, Angelo Badalamenti, and rapid, stellar ascent led to a sudden retreat from the industry where a decade of personal trial ended with a renaissance and reconnection with his work and vocation, documented in a feature film biopic documentary slated for release at the end of this year, executive produced by Tilda Swinton. Last year, he released his seventh album , "rdquo" -> Crying the Neck", an end-of-summer folkloric odyssey set in the landscape at the end of the East of England where Wolf lives and works. The album's success brought him back to his North American audiences; for his first tour in over 13 years, he embarked on a ten-week tour driving himself from east to west coast, where he discovered not only his fanbase had been waiting all that time, but a brand new one had grown in his absence in the States. The success of last year's tour brings Patrick back to North America this year with , "rdquo" -> The Tour of the Beast", this time an extensive East to West coast and back again routing with a coinciding 7" single and release campaign, launching two new songs to the States and ringing in the next era of Patrick Wolf. The first, a bombastic harpsichord banger and outsider anthem , "rdquo" -> The Beast", partly inspired by conversations had in the meet-and-greets of last year's tour and a hymn of solace, initially written as a response to Camus's "The Myth of Sisyphus", a lyre and vocal lullaby called , "rdquo" -> The Laughing Dove". The Guardian - "The Goth Folk Pioneer, A true one off" New York Times - "One of Britains most appealing singer songwriters" Lady Gaga - "Fantastic, Amazing, I listen to him, I meditate" Rolling Stone - "There's nothing not awesome about him" NME - "Britains foremost pop pioneer" Tilda Swinton - , "rdquo" -> My feeling is that we certainly come from the same planet: kith and kin. His music sounds like the great unexpressed soundtrack of a great film I want to see -- and try to catch every night before I go to sleep.."

    The Conversation

    8:00 PM · Astor Place Theatre, Greenwich Village Para salir

    THE CONVERSATION follows Marcus (Tony Award-winner Joshua Henry) and Elle (Julia Harriman) from the electric spark of their first date to move-ins, milestones, and the slow accumulation of everything left unsaid. The score, written by Henry and Harriman, weaves soul, R&B, and modern pop into bold musical theater storytelling that is intimate, honest, and emotionally gripping. With a book by Nick Green and directed by Tony Award-winner Kenny Leon, The Conversation asks what it takes to choose love, even when it hurts, and what it takes to stay.

    Maria Schneider Orchestra

    8:30 PM · Birdland Jazz Club, Hell's Kitchen · $45.76 Algo especial

    Maria Schneiders music has been hailed by critics as evocative, majestic, magical, heart-stoppingly gorgeous, and beyond categorization. She and her 18-member orchestra have performed at concert halls around the world and have received 7 GRAMMYs, many Jazz Journalist Awards, and numerous DOWNBEAT and JAZZTIMES Readers and Critics Polls. Schneiders music blurs the lines between genres, making her long list of commissioners quite varied, stretching from jazz to classical, and dance, even collaborating with David Bowie. She is among a small few to have received GRAMMYs in multiple genres, having received the award in both jazz and classical, as well as for her work with David Bowie. Shes holds honorary doctorates from the University of Minnesota and Eastman School of Music. In 2019, the National Endowment for the Arts bestowed on Schneider the nations highest honor in jazz, naming her an NEA Jazz Master.

    A Ghost in Your Ear

    3:00 PM · Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre, Greenwich Village · ↻ Every Sunday Para salir

    When an actor arrives late to a sound studio for a last-minute audiobook recording session, he is handed the script of a chilling ghost story to read. But as the engineer cues the recording and the evening wears on, the horrors slowly begin to escape the page to haunt the studio itself. Fresh from an acclaimed, sold-out run in London, A GHOST IN YOUR EAR is the "truly terrifying headphone horror" (The Guardian) from the darkly brilliant mind of Tony Award® nominee Jamie Armitage (SIX), made in collaboration with Ben and Max Ringham (ANNA, National Theatre). A mesmerizing blend of gothic horror and psychological thriller, this cutting-edge theatrical experience uses groundbreaking binaural sound technology to immerse every audience member in a haunting world of sound. And at Audible's Minetta Lane Theatre - one of New York's most intimate venues - there's no escaping the frights. Enter if you dare.
